{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"[section-team supervisor]
You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small task: about 50 lines of new code or less (one or two small functions): build it and its tests yourself, then run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Give each spec requirement a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples. Wake nobody. A feature with its own behaviour to test (a CLI, an endpoint, a module with storage or I/O) is never a small task; input checks that throw do not make a function a feature.
- Single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema), above that and up to about 600 lines of new code: build the code yourself (and any README it asks for), then wake only the testing section to write and run the tests (give it the files, the behaviour to cover and the spec's edge cases, and ask it to probe every spec line), then run the reviewer gate on your own changed files before you call it done; testing gates its own test files. Wake no builder section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder plus the testing section for tests and final verification, and add the docs section when the task asks for docs or a README. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files (Opus; do not pass `model`). It ends with a GRADE block. Pass: overall at least 8 and no item under 6.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 2 fix rounds. Then tell the user the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Balanced mode (default).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.name: auto-mode-setup
commands.description: Teach auto mode about your environment, plus optional rule tweaks

commands.name: autocompact
commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

commands.description: Start a new session with empty context; previous session stays on disk (resumable with /resume)

commands.name: color
commands.description: Set the prompt bar color for this session

commands.name: compact
commands.description: Free up context by summarizing the conversation so far

commands.name: config
commands.description: Set a setting by key

commands.name: output-style
commands.description: List output styles or switch to one

commands.name: context
commands.description: Show current context usage

commands.name: effort
commands.description: Set effort level for model usage

commands.name: fast
commands.description: Toggle fast mode (Opus 5.5)

commands.name: focus
commands.description: Toggle focus view: just your prompt, summary, and response

commands.name: heapdump
commands.description: Dump the JS heap to the Desktop; on Linux with no Desktop folder, the home directory

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Manage MCP servers

commands.name: import
commands.description: Import config from another AI coding agent

commands.name: model
commands.description: Set the AI model for Claude Code

commands.name: __remote-workflow
commands.description: Run the workflow script delivered in this session environment (server-launched sessions only)

commands.name: workflow-launch-exec
commands.description: Execute a server-launched workflow handoff (workflow_launch event sessions only)

commands.name: reload-plugins
commands.description: Activate pending plugin changes in the current session

commands.name: reload-skills
commands.description: Pick up skills added or changed on disk during this session

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current conversation

commands.name: ultrareview
commands.description: Start a cloud agent that finds and verifies bugs in your branch (~5-15 min, $5-$25 USD) · Runs in a cloud session. See https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web

commands.name: security-review
commands.description: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

commands.name: usage
commands.description: Show session cost, plan usage, and what's contributing to your limits

commands.name: insights
commands.description: Generate a report analyzing your Claude Code sessions

commands.name: recap
commands.description: Generate a one-line session recap now

commands.name: skill-doctor
commands.description: Show which loaded skills are unused and costing context

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Set a goal — keep working until the condition is met

commands.name: design-consent
commands.description: Grant Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-revoke
commands.description: Revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: list-agents
commands.description: List subagents, teammates, and other Claude sessions you can message

commands.name: team-onboarding
commands.description: Help teammates ramp on Claude Code with a guide from your usage

commands.name: team
commands.description: Show the Team Board, or set this project's mode: /team mode lean|balanced|max

commands.name: chats
commands.description: Show every open chat as a card

Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. # File layout (owner: supervisor) — 2026-11-03

- `server.mjs` — backend. The whole HTTP server. Serves `GET /` from `public/index.html` and `GET /app.js` from `public/app.js`, both resolved relative to the folder of `server.mjs` (via `import.meta.url`), NOT the cwd. Files are read per request (not at startup — startup order is PORT check, data file, listen). A read failure → 500 `internal error` JSON.
- `public/index.html`, `public/app.js` — frontend. Must contain no `http://` / `https://` at all (not even in comments).
- `test/*.test.mjs` — testing. `package.json` "test": `node --test test/`.
- `package.json` — backend creates it: `{"name":"room-bookings","private":true,"type":"module","scripts":{"start":"node server.mjs","test":"node --test test/"}}`.
- `README.md` — docs.
- Data file layout: backend's choice, documented in `.team/notes/data-file.md` by backend.

content.content: # Team notes — one line per note: — — — spec.md — supervisor — full verbatim spec of the booking app (server, API, rules, page) — 2026-11-03 layout.md — supervisor — file layout: server.mjs, public/index.html, public/app.js, test/, package.json — 2026-11-03 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. ## Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

Other query parameters are ignored.

When the page loads, the script requests `GET /api/rooms` and fills `#room` with one `<option>` per room, in that order, whose value and text are the room name. If that request gets an error status, `#error` shows the reply's error message and `#room` stays empty; with no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and `#room` stays empty. The first list fetch starts at page load too, without waiting for the rooms reply.

Each `<li>` has exactly two child nodes: a text node with exactly the text `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` and no trailing space (for example `2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 Aurora: Standup`), then a `<button type="button">` with the text `Cancel`. With no bookings, the list holds a single `<li>` whose only child is a text node `No bookings.`.

When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.

Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.

- A list fetch that gets an error status shows the reply's error message in `#error` and leaves the list as it was; one that gets no reply shows `Could not reach the server.` and leaves the list as it was; one that succeeds leaves `#error` alone. When list fetches overlap, only the outcome of the last one started is used: the outcome of every earlier one, an error status or no reply included, changes neither the list nor `#error`.
- Booking: a submit event on the form never reloads the page (the script calls `preventDefault`). A submit while `Book` is disabled sends nothing. Otherwise the script disables `Book`, then sends `POST /api/bookings` with exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON body whose keys `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end` hold the five controls' current values unchanged (the title is not trimmed). The script never checks the fields itself. `Book` is enabled again as soon as the request settles (the reply and its body have arrived, or the request failed), before anything else happens. On 201 the `title` control is emptied (the others keep their values), `#error` is emptied and the list is fetched again. On any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message exactly (for example `room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`). With no reply `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.`. In both of these cases the form and the list stay as they were.
- Cancel: clicking a `Cancel` button disables it and sends `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` for its booking; the button is enabled again when the request settles. On 204 `#error` is emptied; on any other status `#error` shows the reply's error message (for example `booking not found` when the booking was already gone). After either of these, the list is fetched again. With no reply, `#error` shows `Could not reach the server.` and the list is not fetched again.
- Filter: a `change` event on `#filter-date` fetches the list again at once; the `input` event does nothing. `Show all` sets the value of `#filter-date` to the empty string and fetches the list again once, without dispatching any event.

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. One Node.js file (`server.mjs`) serves a
JSON API and a browser page, and keeps every booking in a single JSON file.

There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later.
- No dependencies. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so there is nothing to
  `npm install`.

## Running the server

```sh
npm start
# or
node server.mjs
```

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is listening it prints one
line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Must be ASCII digits only and at most 65535. `0` lets the OS choose a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |

An unset or empty variable uses its default.

Examples:

```sh
PORT=8080 node server.mjs
PORT=0 node server.mjs                      # OS picks the port
DATA_FILE=/var/data/rooms.json npm start
DATA_FILE=data/bookings.json PORT=4000 npm start
```

### Startup and exit codes

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
listening. It exits with code 1, after writing one line to stderr, when:

- `PORT` is not made only of digits, is above 65535, or cannot be bound
  (for example because it is already in use);
- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
  (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not valid data
  (for example empty or not JSON). The message is then
  `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.

A data file that does not exist (or whose folder does not exist) simply means
there are no bookings yet.

### The data file

The data file is JSON managed by the server. Keep these points in mind:

- It is read once, at startup. Changes made to it from outside while the
  server runs are not noticed.
- It is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each change is
  saved before the reply is sent. After a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`,
  the bookings and the next booking id are the same as before.
- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example the folder
  does not exist), the request gets `500 internal error`, nothing changes, and
  the server keeps running.

## The browser page

Open `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` (or whichever port you chose). The page has:

- a form (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, then **Book**) that creates a booking;
- a booking list, with a **Cancel** button next to each booking;
- a **Show date** filter that shows only the bookings on one date, and a
  **Show all** button that clears it;
- an error line that shows the server's error message (or
  `Could not reach the server.` when there is no reply).

The page itself does no validation: every check is made by the server, and
its error message is shown as is. The page loads its script from `/app.js`.

## API

All paths are matched exactly, byte for byte: no percent-decoding, no
case folding, no trailing-slash or dot-segment normalisation. The query
string is ignored unless a route says otherwise.

Every JSON reply has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An
error reply is always:

```json
{ "error": "<message>" }
```

### Bookings

A booking is a JSON object with exactly these keys:

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "room": "Aurora",
  "title": "Standup",
  "date": "2026-11-03",
  "start": "09:00",
  "end": "10:00"
}
```

`id` is a number; the other fields are strings. The first booking gets id 1
and every new booking the next integer. Ids are never reused, even after
deletes and restarts.

### Routes

| Method   | Path                  | Success |
|----------|-----------------------|---------|
| `GET`    | `/api/rooms`          | `200 {"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` |
| `GET`    | `/api/bookings`       | `200 {"bookings": [...]}` |
| `POST`   | `/api/bookings`       | `201` with the new booking |
| `DELETE` | `/api/bookings/<id>`  | `204` with an empty body |
| `GET`    | `/`                   | `200` the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) |
| `GET`    | `/app.js`             | `200` the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) |

#### `GET /api/bookings`

Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start time, then room (in the
order Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos).

With a `date` query parameter, only the bookings on that date are returned.
`?date` with no value counts as the empty value; when `date` is repeated, the
first one is used. Other query parameters are ignored.

- `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` when the `date` value is not a
  valid date (see rule 6 below), the empty value included.

#### `POST /api/bookings`

Send `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON object with `room`, `title`,
`date`, `start` and `end`. Other keys are ignored. The reply is `201` and the
new booking.

#### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`

Deletes the booking. Any path of the form `/api/bookings/<id>`, where `<id>`
is non-empty and holds no `/`, is this route.

- `404 booking not found` when `<id>` is not a positive integer written in
  digits without a leading zero (for example `abc`, `0`, `01`), or no booking
  has that id.

### Booking rules

`POST /api/bookings` checks these rules in order; the first one that fails
decides the reply.

| # | Rule | Reply |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type (before any `;`, case-insensitive) must be `application/json` | `415 content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | The body must be at most 10000 bytes | `413 body too large` |
| 3 | The body must be a JSON object (not empty, invalid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean) | `400 body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` must be exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | `400 room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` must be a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends | `400 title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400 start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400 end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` must be later than `start` | `400 end must be after start` |
| 10 | The booking must not overlap another booking of the same room on the same date | `409 room is already booked from <start> to <end>` |

Notes:

- The title is stored trimmed. No other field is trimmed or changed, so
  ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are all invalid.
- Two bookings overlap when each starts before the other ends. A booking may
  start exactly when another ends. The 409 message names the start and end of
  the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- Requests sent at the same time behave as if handled one at a time: of
  several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the
  others get 409.

### Other errors

| Reply | When |
|-------|------|
| `404 not found` | Any other path, whatever the method. This includes `/api/bookings/` and paths such as `/api/bookings/1/`. |
| `405 method not allowed` | A known path with a method it does not support, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` included. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` or `PUT /api/rooms`. |
| `500 internal error` | Saving the data file failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |

### curl examples

```sh
# List the rooms
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms

# Create a booking
curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
# HTTP/1.1 201 Created
# {"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}

# The same slot again is a conflict
curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Retro","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:30","end":"10:30"}'
# HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
# {"error":"room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00"}

# List all bookings, or only one date
curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'

# Delete a booking
curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

## Running the tests

The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner:

```sh
npm test
# which runs: node --test test/
```

## File layout

```
server.mjs          HTTP server: JSON API, page serving, data file handling
public/index.html   The browser page (served at /)
public/app.js       The page script (served at /app.js)
test/*.test.mjs     Tests (node:test)
package.json        "type": "module"; "start" and "test" scripts
bookings.json       Default data file, created on the first booking (in the cwd)
```

`public/` is resolved relative to the folder of `server.mjs`, so the page
works whatever the current working directory is. The data file, by contrast,
is resolved against the current working directory.

# Data file layout (owner: backend) — 2026-11-03

File: `DATA_FILE` env (unset/empty → `bookings.json`), resolved against the cwd.
UTF-8 JSON, written by `server.mjs` only on a successful POST create or DELETE.

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "x", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "10:00", "end": "11:00" }
  ]
}
```

Strict validation at startup (anything else → stderr `cannot read data file <name>`, exit 1):
- Top level: an object with exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`.
- `nextId`: a safe integer ≥ 1, the id the next booking gets (never reused).
- `bookings`: an array (any order). Each entry has exactly the keys `id, room, title, date, start, end`:
  - `id` a safe integer, 1 ≤ id < nextId, unique.
  - `room` one of Aurora/Borealis/Cosmos; `title` a string already trimmed, 1–80 UTF-16 units.
  - `date` valid per booking rule 6; `start`/`end` valid `HH:MM`, start < end.
  - No two bookings overlap (same room + date, each starts before the other ends).
- Read errors: `ENOENT` → no bookings, nextId 1 (file not created). Any other read error → exit 1.

Fixtures for tests: write `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}` for an empty store, or let the file be missing.
An empty file, invalid JSON, a BOM or a directory path all make startup fail.

- **Startup:** the steps run in order (PORT, then data file, then listen).
- **PORT:** values are checked as digits only and at most 65535; empty or unset means 3000; listen failures (port in use, EACCES) go through the `error` handler to exit 1.
- **Data file:** ENOENT means no bookings, and any other read error or bad layout gives the exact `cannot read data file <name>` message. `<name>` is the value as given, and the path is resolved against the cwd.
- **Routing:**
  - The path is cut at the first `?` and compared byte for byte.
  - `/api/bookings/<id>` gives 404 `not found` for an empty id or one holding `/`, and 405 for any method other than DELETE.
  - HEAD and OPTIONS get 405.
  - The page files are looked up with `hasOwn`, so `/__proto__` cannot match.
- **Rules 1–10:** checked in order. The Content-Type check trims spaces and tabs only, ignores ASCII case only, and runs before 413. The size check counts every received byte while keeping only about 10 KB in memory. The 409 reply uses the earliest-starting clash.
- **Date filter:** `?date` with no value gives 400, and repeated `date` uses the first value.
- **DELETE ids:** must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`, and are compared with `String(id)`, so huge or leading-zero ids give 404.
- **Concurrency:** creates and deletes run one at a time through a promise chain. Validation runs outside the lock, which is fine because it does not read the stored bookings.
- **Save failures:** memory is updated only after the write succeeds (`commit`, lines 196-199), so a failed save gives 500 and leaves the next id unchanged.
- **Request bodies:** fully read before every reply.
- **stdout:** the listening line is the only thing written there.

1. **One-line stderr rule (spec conformance, edge case)**, `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:325`. `fail(\`invalid PORT ${process.env.PORT}\`)` copies the raw value into the message. A PORT holding a newline or other control character prints more than one line on stderr, but the spec requires exactly one. The data file message (line 330) is fixed by the spec, so it is not affected.
2. **Saves are not atomic**, `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/server.mjs:133-136`. `writeFile` truncates the file and then writes into it. A failure partway through (ENOSPC, or the process being killed) leaves a half-written file. Memory stays unchanged, but the next startup then fails with `cannot read data file`, which goes against "nothing changes" and the persistence guarantee. Writing a sibling temp file and then renaming it avoids this, and creates no folders.
3. **Duplicated message**, lines 73 and 206: the string `'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'` appears twice. Make it one constant so the validator and the date filter can't drift apart.
4. **Unclear helper**, lines 254-256, 266, 277, 281: `methodNotAllowed()` throws, but at line 272 it is written as `return methodNotAllowed()` and elsewhere as a bare statement. A name like `throwMethodNotAllowed`, or using `throw new HttpError(405, …)` directly, would make the control flow plain.

# Shared decisions (append only): date — section — decision — why

- 2026-11-03 — backend — Data file layout `{nextId, bookings[]}`, validated strictly at startup (exact keys, valid fields, unique ids < nextId, no overlaps); see data-file.md — stricter reading of "content is not data in the layout this server writes".
- 2026-11-03 — backend — Saves write `<DATA_FILE>.<pid>.tmp` then rename it over the data file; memory changes only after the rename succeeds — an interrupted save never corrupts the file, and a failed save leaves state and next id unchanged.
- 2026-11-03 — backend — Content-Type media type folds ASCII A-Z only; trims only spaces and tabs — exact reading of rule 1.
# Data file layout (owner: backend) — 2026-11-03

File: `DATA_FILE` env (unset/empty → `bookings.json`), resolved against the cwd.
UTF-8 JSON, written by `server.mjs` only on a successful POST create or DELETE.

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "x", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "10:00", "end": "11:00" }
  ]
}
```

Strict validation at startup (anything else → stderr `cannot read data file <name>`, exit 1):
- Top level: an object with exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`.
- `nextId`: a safe integer ≥ 1, the id the next booking gets (never reused).
- `bookings`: an array (any order). Each entry has exactly the keys `id, room, title, date, start, end`:
  - `id` a safe integer, 1 ≤ id < nextId, unique.
  - `room` one of Aurora/Borealis/Cosmos; `title` a string already trimmed, 1–80 UTF-16 units.
  - `date` valid per booking rule 6; `start`/`end` valid `HH:MM`, start < end.
  - No two bookings overlap (same room + date, each starts before the other ends).
- Read errors: `ENOENT` → no bookings, nextId 1 (file not created). Any other read error → exit 1.

Fixtures for tests: write `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}` for an empty store, or let the file be missing.
An empty file, invalid JSON, a BOM or a directory path all make startup fail.

content.content: # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. ## Server - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. ## API - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. ## Page - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. - The page loads the script with a `

# Data file layout (owner: backend) — 2026-11-03

File: `DATA_FILE` env (unset/empty → `bookings.json`), resolved against the cwd.
UTF-8 JSON, written by `server.mjs` only on a successful POST create or DELETE.

```json
{
  "nextId": 3,
  "bookings": [
    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "x", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "10:00", "end": "11:00" }
  ]
}
```

Strict validation at startup (anything else → stderr `cannot read data file <name>`, exit 1):
- Top level: an object with exactly the keys `nextId` and `bookings`.
- `nextId`: a safe integer ≥ 1, the id the next booking gets (never reused).
- `bookings`: an array (any order). Each entry has exactly the keys `id, room, title, date, start, end`:
  - `id` a safe integer, 1 ≤ id < nextId, unique.
  - `room` one of Aurora/Borealis/Cosmos; `title` a string already trimmed, 1–80 UTF-16 units.
  - `date` valid per booking rule 6; `start`/`end` valid `HH:MM`, start < end.
  - No two bookings overlap (same room + date, each starts before the other ends).
- Read errors: `ENOENT` → no bookings, nextId 1 (file not created). Any other read error → exit 1.

Fixtures for tests: write `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}` for an empty store, or let the file be missing.
An empty file, invalid JSON, a BOM or a directory path all make startup fail.
----
# Shared decisions (append only): date — section — decision — why

- 2026-11-03 — backend — Data file layout `{nextId, bookings[]}`, validated strictly at startup (exact keys, valid fields, unique ids < nextId, no overlaps); see data-file.md — stricter reading of "content is not data in the layout this server writes".
- 2026-11-03 — backend — Saves write `<DATA_FILE>.<pid>.tmp` then rename it over the data file; memory changes only after the rename succeeds — an interrupted save never corrupts the file, and a failed save leaves state and next id unchanged.
- 2026-11-03 — backend — Content-Type media type folds ASCII A-Z only; trims only spaces and tabs — exact reading of rule 1.
- 2026-11-03 — frontend — A 200 reply whose body has the wrong shape shows `Request failed.` and leaves the room list and booking list unchanged — the spec does not cover this case; this is the safest reading.

content.content:
1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app. One Node.js file (`server.mjs`) serves a
4	JSON API and a browser page, and keeps every booking in a single JSON file.
5	
6	There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.
7	
8	## Requirements
9	
10	- Node.js 22 or later.
11	- No dependencies. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so there is nothing to
12	  `npm install`.
13	
14	## Running the server
15	
16	```sh
17	npm start
18	# or
19	node server.mjs
20	```
21	
22	The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. Once it is listening it prints one
23	line to stdout:
24	
25	```
26	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
27	```
28	
29	### Environment variables
30	
31	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
32	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
33	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Must be ASCII digits only and at most 65535. `0` lets the OS choose a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
34	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the data file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |
35	
36	An unset or empty variable uses its default.
37	
38	Examples:
39	
40	```sh
41	PORT=8080 node server.mjs
42	PORT=0 node server.mjs                      # OS picks the port
43	DATA_FILE=/var/data/rooms.json npm start
44	DATA_FILE=data/bookings.json PORT=4000 npm start
45	```
46	
47	### Startup and exit codes
48	
49	At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
50	listening. It exits with code 1, after writing one line to stderr, when:
51	
52	- `PORT` is not made only of digits, is above 65535, or cannot be bound
53	  (for example because it is already in use);
54	- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
55	  (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not valid data
56	  (for example empty or not JSON). The message is then
57	  `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.
58	
59	A data file that does not exist (or whose folder does not exist) simply means
60	there are no bookings yet.
61	
62	### The data file
63	
64	The data file is UTF-8 JSON managed by the server. It holds the id the next
65	booking will get and the list of bookings:
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "nextId": 3,
70	  "bookings": [
71	    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
72	  ]
73	}
74	```
75	
76	At startup the server checks the content strictly. The top level must have
77	exactly the keys `nextId` (an integer, at least 1) and `bookings` (an array).
78	Each booking must have exactly the six booking keys and follow the booking
79	rules: a known room, a trimmed title of 1 to 80 characters, a valid date and
80	times, and `start` before `end`. Each id must be unique and below `nextId`,
81	and no two bookings may overlap. Anything else, including an empty file,
82	invalid JSON or a byte order mark, stops startup with
83	`cannot read data file <name>`. To start with an empty store, delete the file
84	or write `{"nextId":1,"bookings":[]}`.
85	
86	Keep these points in mind:
87	
88	- It is read once, at startup. Changes made to it from outside while the
89	  server runs are not noticed.
90	- It is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each change is
91	  saved before the reply is sent. After a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`,
92	  the bookings and the next booking id are the same as before.
93	- A save writes a temporary file `<DATA_FILE>.<pid>.tmp` next to the data
94	  file and then renames it over the data file. An interrupted save therefore
95	  never leaves a half-written data file.
96	- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example the folder
97	  does not exist), the request gets `500 internal error`, nothing changes, and
98	  the server keeps running.
99	
100	## The browser page
101	
102	Open `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` (or whichever port you chose). The page has:
103	
104	- a form (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, then **Book**) that creates a booking;
105	- a booking list, with a **Cancel** button next to each booking;
106	- a **Show date** filter that shows only the bookings on one date, and a
107	  **Show all** button that clears it;
108	- an error line that shows the server's error message, or
109	  `Could not reach the server.` when there is no reply. If a reply has an
110	  unexpected shape, it shows `Request failed.` instead.
111	
112	The page itself does no validation: every check is made by the server, and
113	its error message is shown as is. The page loads its script from `/app.js`.
114	
115	## API
116	
117	All paths are matched exactly, byte for byte: no percent-decoding, no
118	case folding, no trailing-slash or dot-segment normalisation. The query
119	string is ignored unless a route says otherwise.
120	
121	Every JSON reply has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An
122	error reply is always:
123	
124	```json
125	{ "error": "<message>" }
126	```
127	
128	### Bookings
129	
130	A booking is a JSON object with exactly these keys:
131	
132	```json
133	{
134	  "id": 1,
135	  "room": "Aurora",
136	  "title": "Standup",
137	  "date": "2026-11-03",
138	  "start": "09:00",
139	  "end": "10:00"
140	}
141	```
142	
143	`id` is a number; the other fields are strings. The first booking gets id 1
144	and every new booking the next integer. Ids are never reused, even after
145	deletes and restarts.
146	
147	### Routes
148	
149	| Method   | Path                  | Success |
150	|----------|-----------------------|---------|
151	| `GET`    | `/api/rooms`          | `200 {"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` |
152	| `GET`    | `/api/bookings`       | `200 {"bookings": [...]}` |
153	| `POST`   | `/api/bookings`       | `201` with the new booking |
154	| `DELETE` | `/api/bookings/<id>`  | `204` with an empty body |
155	| `GET`    | `/`                   | `200` the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) |
156	| `GET`    | `/app.js`             | `200` the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) |
157	
158	#### `GET /api/bookings`
159	
160	Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start time, then room (in the
161	order Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos).
162	
163	With a `date` query parameter, only the bookings on that date are returned.
164	`?date` with no value counts as the empty value; when `date` is repeated, the
165	first one is used. Other query parameters are ignored.
166	
167	- `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` when the `date` value is not a
168	  valid date (see rule 6 below), the empty value included.
169	
170	#### `POST /api/bookings`
171	
172	Send `Content-Type: application/json` and a JSON object with `room`, `title`,
173	`date`, `start` and `end`. Other keys are ignored. The reply is `201` and the
174	new booking.
175	
176	#### `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>`
177	
178	Deletes the booking. Any path of the form `/api/bookings/<id>`, where `<id>`
179	is non-empty and holds no `/`, is this route.
180	
181	- `404 booking not found` when `<id>` is not a positive integer written in
182	  digits without a leading zero (for example `abc`, `0`, `01`), or no booking
183	  has that id.
184	
185	### Booking rules
186	
187	`POST /api/bookings` checks these rules in order; the first one that fails
188	decides the reply.
189	
190	| # | Rule | Reply |
191	|---|------|-------|
192	| 1 | The `Content-Type` media type (before any `;`, case-insensitive) must be `application/json` | `415 content type must be application/json` |
193	| 2 | The body must be at most 10000 bytes | `413 body too large` |
194	| 3 | The body must be a JSON object (not empty, invalid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean) | `400 body must be a JSON object` |
195	| 4 | `room` must be exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | `400 room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
196	| 5 | `title` must be a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends | `400 title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
197	| 6 | `date` must be `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | `400 date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
198	| 7 | `start` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400 start must be HH:MM` |
199	| 8 | `end` must be `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | `400 end must be HH:MM` |
200	| 9 | `end` must be later than `start` | `400 end must be after start` |
201	| 10 | The booking must not overlap another booking of the same room on the same date | `409 room is already booked from <start> to <end>` |
202	
203	Notes:
204	
205	- The title is stored trimmed. No other field is trimmed or changed, so
206	  ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are all invalid.
207	- Two bookings overlap when each starts before the other ends. A booking may
208	  start exactly when another ends. The 409 message names the start and end of
209	  the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
210	- Requests sent at the same time behave as if handled one at a time: of
211	  several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the
212	  others get 409.
213	
214	### Other errors
215	
216	| Reply | When |
217	|-------|------|
218	| `404 not found` | Any other path, whatever the method. This includes `/api/bookings/` and paths such as `/api/bookings/1/`. |
219	| `405 method not allowed` | A known path with a method it does not support, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` included. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` or `PUT /api/rooms`. |
220	| `500 internal error` | Saving the data file failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |
221	
222	### curl examples
223	
224	```sh
225	# List the rooms
226	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms
227	
228	# Create a booking
229	curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
230	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
231	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
232	# HTTP/1.1 201 Created
233	# {"id":1,"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}
234	
235	# The same slot again is a conflict
236	curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
237	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
238	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Retro","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:30","end":"10:30"}'
239	# HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
240	# {"error":"room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00"}
241	
242	# List all bookings, or only one date
243	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
244	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'
245	
246	# Delete a booking
247	curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
248	# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
249	```
250	
251	## Running the tests
252	
253	The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner:
254	
255	```sh
256	npm test
257	# which runs: node --test test/
258	```
259	
260	## File layout
261	
262	```
263	server.mjs          HTTP server: JSON API, page serving, data file handling
264	public/index.html   The browser page (served at /)
265	public/app.js       The page script (served at /app.js)
266	test/*.test.mjs     Tests (node:test)
267	package.json        "type": "module"; "start" and "test" scripts
268	bookings.json       Default data file, created on the first booking (in the cwd)
269	```
270	
271	`public/` is resolved relative to the folder of `server.mjs`, so the page
272	works whatever the current working directory is. The data file, by contrast,
273	is resolved against the current working directory.
274
